prompt: Create a transparent orthographic atlas in exactly two columns by two rows. Use reference image 1 only for row 1, the scrap-metal EDGE transition; use reference image 2 only for row 2, the scrap-metal CORNER transition. In each row, column 1 is RIGHT and column 2 is LEFT, strict level horizontal side elevation. The references are the actual source tile crops; preserve their exact rusted orange/red/gray steel, bolts, rails and hazard stripes. Do not redraw the source top view. These are SIDE elevations of a flat floor tile. Show a very thin horizontal slab profile with visible metal thickness, and the safety rail as a horizontal bar at its correct upper world-Z height. For the EDGE row, the rail should be seen end-on from the right/left: a short horizontal cap at the proper end of the shallow slab, not a tall post and not a broad horizontal span. For the CORNER row, the source has a rail along two adjacent plan edges; in right and left elevations show one broad horizontal rail bar at shared Z, with the adjoining edge rail end visible only if physically at that end. Never turn an L-shaped plan into an upright L silhouette. No overhead square panel, no full tile face, no perspective, no vertical rail, no missing height. Center exactly one horizontal edge profile per cell with substantial transparent gutters. Inferred projections, not recovered pixels or calibrated 3D.
geometry_constraints: thin horizontal slab with rail at shared Z
edge rail end-on, no tall post
corner rail remains horizontal, no upright L
